narrative.primer: Narrative and audio roles write the words, characters, and sounds, and fit them to what the systems allow. With an in-game agent, they also write the agent's voice and the limits of what it may say.

scope.label: Narrative scope
scope.value: Captions and translations from Davis 1894 for each built level; descriptions, instructions, feedback, success lines and Hint ladders in the JSON; every line at most three rows (about 180 characters), reachable, and cited when it comes from a source

sound.label: Sound vocabulary
sound.value: Built: the haul's drum and pull tones (synthesised in haul.gd) and a Sound volume setting. No music or other effects before G2; background music that can be turned off and sound effects after

voice.label: Agent voice and limits
voice.value: Min: anxious and fussy, frets over the Negative Confession, one short line when clicked; never names the fix, his target piece or its destination; facts only by fact_id from the entries he may see (Configuration Document, Section 4)

narrative.subtitle: Captions, descriptions, hints, citations, Min's voice, sound

qa.primer: QA checks what the game does against what it should do, reproduces failures so someone else can see them, and verifies fixes. QA reports; it never decides what ships. It writes tests and reports; tech fixes.

blocking.label: What counts as a blocking bug
blocking.value: A crash or script error, a level or minigame that cannot be finished or left, a soft lock (an object lost, hands stuck full, the camera stuck in minigame view), lost progress, or Min revealing a solution the player has not reached

rules.label: Rule-change check
rules.value: On any change to a rule, a control or the player interface, sort its details as check-features step 1 and send every unstated one to the student; never accept it by default
